rationale: The verify workflow already implements the optimizations the evidence supports for this job shape: (1) dependency caching via setup-node `cache: npm` keyed on all three lockfiles (root, workflow-scripts, docs), so P-LIT-GHA-CACHE's equivalent cache already exists, which is a listed contraindication for adding another cache; (2) an explicit job timeout (`timeout-minutes: 30`) already bounds the job, so P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT's scenario (adding a timeout where none existed) does not apply, and the measured experiment is not a valid basis for tightening an existing bound given only five warm-cache runs and the cold-install/slow-valid-run safety tests; (3) stale-run cancellation is already present via `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE). The remaining patterns are not applicable or contraindicated: no matrix (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST), no schedule (P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE), test/build selection would reduce required-check coverage (P-LIT-SELECT, P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT, P-LIT-PRIORITIZE), path filtering is risky because shared root config/generators affect docs and workflow-scripts (P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER), and environment/distributed/incremental-cache patterns require infrastructure or unverified assumptions. All build/test coverage is preserved, so no change is supported.
